chapters.title: The Gospel Is God's Power
chapters.synopsis: Paul introduces himself to the saints at Rome as an apostle set apart for the gospel and declares he is not ashamed of it, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes. He then describes how the gentile world, refusing to honor the God plainly revealed in creation, has descended into idolatry and every kind of unrighteousness.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Greeting; the gospel's power; the gentile world condemned

chapters.title: God Judges Without Respect of Persons
chapters.synopsis: Paul warns that those who judge others while doing the same things store up wrath for themselves, for God will render to every man according to his deeds. Possessing the law or the name of Jew is not enough; true circumcision is of the heart, and the doers of the law are justified rather than the hearers.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: God's impartial judgment of Jew and gentile alike

chapters.title: All Have Sinned, Justified Freely
chapters.synopsis: Paul concludes that Jews and gentiles alike are all under sin, so that no flesh is justified by the deeds of the law. God's righteousness now comes by faith in Jesus Christ, whose atoning sacrifice justifies sinners freely by grace, leaving no room for boasting.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: All under sin; justification by grace through faith

chapters.title: Abraham Justified by Faith
chapters.synopsis: Paul shows that Abraham was counted righteous because he believed God, long before circumcision or the law, and that David likewise described the blessedness of forgiven sin. Abraham, who staggered not at God's promise despite his age, becomes the father of all who believe.

chapters.title: Peace with God Through Christ
chapters.synopsis: Being justified by faith, believers have peace with God and rejoice even in tribulation, for God proved his love in that Christ died for us while we were yet sinners. As sin and death entered the world through one man, Adam, so righteousness and life abound to many through one man, Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Peace through justification; Adam and Christ contrasted

chapters.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
chapters.synopsis: Paul teaches that those baptized into Christ are baptized into his death and raised to walk in newness of life, so they must not continue in sin that grace may abound. Freed from sin, believers become servants of righteousness, for the wages of sin is death but the gift of God is eternal life.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Baptism into newness of life; servants of righteousness

chapters.title: The Law and the Inner Struggle
chapters.synopsis: Paul explains that believers are dead to the law through the body of Christ, as a widow is freed from the law of her husband. He describes the anguished struggle of the divided self, willing what is good yet doing what he hates, and cries out for deliverance through Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Freed from the law; the war within

chapters.title: Life in the Spirit
chapters.synopsis: There is now no condemnation to those in Christ Jesus who walk after the Spirit, by whom believers cry Abba, Father, as joint-heirs with Christ. Paul declares that all things work together for good to them that love God, and that nothing in creation can separate the saints from the love of God in Christ.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: No condemnation; nothing separates us from God's love

chapters.title: God's Purpose Concerning Israel
chapters.synopsis: Paul grieves for his kinsmen Israel and reviews how God's promise has always run through chosen lines, from Isaac to Jacob, for the children of the promise are counted as the seed. God, like a potter over the clay, shows mercy on whom he will, and has called a people from among both Jews and gentiles.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Sorrow for Israel; the children of promise

chapters.title: Faith Comes by Hearing
chapters.synopsis: Paul testifies that Israel has a zeal for God without knowledge, seeking to establish its own righteousness instead of the righteousness of faith. Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, yet none can call without hearing, nor hear without a preacher, for faith comes by hearing the word of God.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Righteousness by faith; beautiful feet of preachers

chapters.title: A Remnant of Israel Preserved
chapters.synopsis: Paul insists God has not cast away his people, for as in Elijah's day a faithful remnant remains according to the election of grace. Using the figure of an olive tree, he warns the grafted-in gentiles not to boast against the natural branches, for Israel's blindness is partial and temporary, and all Israel shall be saved.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: The remnant; olive tree; all Israel saved

chapters.title: A Living Sacrifice of Love
chapters.synopsis: Paul beseeches the saints to present their bodies a living sacrifice and to be transformed by the renewing of their minds rather than conformed to the world. As one body with many members exercising differing gifts, they are to love without hypocrisy, bless their persecutors, and overcome evil with good.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Living sacrifice; many members, one body; sincere love

chapters.title: Love Fulfils the Law
chapters.synopsis: Paul counsels the saints to be subject to governing powers and to render taxes, custom, fear, and honor where they are due. All the commandments are summed up in loving one's neighbor as oneself, and knowing the night is far spent, believers should cast off the works of darkness and put on the Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Subjection to authority; love fulfils the law

chapters.title: Receive the Weak in Faith
chapters.synopsis: Paul urges the strong not to despise nor judge those with scruples about food and holy days, for every servant stands or falls to his own master and each will answer to God. The kingdom of God is not meat and drink but righteousness, peace, and joy, so no one should put a stumbling block in a brother's way.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Do not judge a brother over meat and days

chapters.title: Christ, the Hope of All Nations
chapters.synopsis: Paul teaches that the strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, following Christ who pleased not himself, and cites the prophets to show that the gentiles were always meant to glorify God. He describes his own ministry from Jerusalem round about to Illyricum and his plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain after carrying a collection to the poor saints at Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Gentile hope; Paul's ministry and travel plans

chapters.title: Greetings and Final Benediction
chapters.synopsis: Paul commends Phebe and sends warm greetings to a long roll of fellow laborers in Rome, including Priscilla and Aquila who risked their own necks for his life. He warns the saints to mark and avoid those who cause divisions, and closes with praise to God who is able to establish them according to the gospel.
